Description: implicit — interpolate-hcl drops the layer on Native before android-v13.7.1
prompt: One style JSON, shared between our web app (MapLibre GL JS) and our Android app (MapLibre Native, org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk 13.6.1). On Android this layer never draws, while every other layer in the style is fine and there is no crash: `{"id": "density", "type": "fill", "source": "tracts", "source-layer": "tracts", "paint": {"fill-color": ["interpolate-hcl", ["linear"], ["get", "density"], 0, "#f7fbff", 5000, "#08306b"]}}`. The same style is correct in the browser. Where do I look?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**What you’re seeing is the classic “layer is silently dropped because the paint expression can’t be parsed” symptom.** In Android SDK 13.6.1 the `interpolate-hcl` (and `interpolate-lab`) expressions are **not yet implemented**. When the style parser meets an unknown expression it discards the whole layer – no crash, no warning in the UI, only a single log line like: ``` [ParseStyle]: value must be a string ``` That is exactly what you’re observing: every other layer draws, the *density* fill never appears. ### How to fix it | Option | What to do | When it works | |--------|------------|---------------| | **Upgrade the Native SDK** | Move to **android-v13.7.1** (or any later release). The PR that added `interpolate-hcl`/`interpolate-lab` is #4668 and was shipped in 13.7.1. | The layer will render exactly as it does in GL JS. | | **Stay on 13.6.1 and replace the expression** | Use a plain `interpolate` with intermediate stops (or a linear ramp) that you write in JSON, e.g.:
```json
"fill-color": [
"interpolate", ["linear"], ["get", "density"],
0, "#f7fbff",
1250, "#c6dbef",
2500, "#6baed6",
3750, "#2171b5",
5000, "#08306b"
]
``` | Works on any Native version because `interpolate` (linear) has always been supported. | | **Add a fallback for older releases** | Keep the `interpolate-hcl` for browsers, but programmatically detect the Android SDK version and swap the paint value at runtime (e.g. via `style.getLayer("density")?.setProperties(...)`). | Gives you the best visual on newer devices while still working on older ones. | ### Where to look / verify 1. **Logcat** – after the map loads, filter for `ParseStyle`. You should see a line similar to: ``` D/MapLibre: [ParseStyle] value must be a string (layer: density, property: fill-color) ``` That confirms the parser rejected the expression. 2. **Style inspection** – in your Kotlin code you can dump the style after it’s loaded: ```kotlin mapboxMap.getStyle { style -> Log.d("Style", style.toJson()) } ``` The `fill-color` entry for the `density` layer will be missing (or set to the default). 3. **Version check** – confirm the SDK you’re using: ```kotlin Log.i("MapLibre", "SDK version: ${MapLibre.getVersion()}") ``` If it prints `13.6.1`, you need the upgrade. ### Recommended next steps 1. **Upgrade**: Add the latest Maven coordinate (as of Oct 2026) to your `build.gradle`: ```gradle implementation "org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.7.1" ``` Re-build and run – the `density` layer should now appear with the HCL-interpolated colors. 2. **If you can’t upgrade** (e.g., corporate policy or device constraints), replace the expression with a standard `interpolate` ramp as shown above, or generate the HCL-based ramp ahead of time and embed the stops manually. 3. **Test on a clean device**: Clear the app’s cache or uninstall/reinstall to make sure no old style JSON is being cached. --- **Bottom line:** `interpolate-hcl` is not supported in Android SDK 13.6.1, so the layer is dropped. Upgrade to 13.7.1 (or later) or fall back to a plain `interpolate` ramp. Once you do that, the style will render identically on both the web and the Android app.
